## What you will learn
Reproducible research requires more than shared code. It connects well-managed data, versioned analyses, computational environments and documented results. 
Through this [course]{.content-visible unless-profile="workshop"}[workshop]{.content-visible when-profile="workshop"} you will learn to:

::::: {.home-goal}
:::: {.home-goal-list}
- **Organize** a project, and keep the raw data untouched
- **Track** every change with Git and collaborate through GitHub
- **Lock** the software dependencies with Pixi, and ship in containers
- **Report** results with Quarto and Jupyter (literate programming)
- **Automate** the pipeline with Snakemake and Nextflow
- **Share** your work with an open license, and archive it on Zenodo
::::

:::: {.home-goal-card}
[The goal]{.home-card-kicker}

[From raw data to results anyone can reproduce]{.home-goal-title}

::: {.home-flow}
1. []{.bi .bi-file-earmark-code aria-hidden="true"} Data & code
2. []{.bi .bi-box-seam aria-hidden="true"} Environment & workflow
3. []{.bi .bi-graph-up-arrow aria-hidden="true"} Results
:::

::: {.home-command}
[\$]{.home-prompt} `pixi run reproduce`
:::
::::
:::::

## Who it is for

Graduate students, postdocs and researchers who analyse data with code, in
genomics, biology or any other field. You need some experience with Python or
R, and basic comfort with a terminal: if it is new to you, an hour of
[Bash 101](pages/C-bash.qmd) gets you there. No genomics or Git experience is
needed.

##  Project-based learning
Learn through a guided genomics project, then apply the skills to your own research.

::::: {.home-cards .home-cards-2}
:::: {.home-card .home-project}
[Guided genomics project]{.home-card-kicker}

### The LTEE project

Work with genomic data from the [Long-Term Evolution Experiment](pages/ltee-project.qmd) to develop an automated and reproducible variant analysis workflow.

[[]{.bi .bi-question-circle aria-hidden="true"} The question[How many mutations did *E. coli* accumulate over 50,000 generations, and is that answer robust to how strictly we filter the variant calls?]{#ltee-question .home-question-text role="tooltip"}]{.home-question tabindex="0" aria-describedby="ltee-question"}
[[More about the project ](assessment/ltee-project.qmd){.home-card-link}]{.content-visible when-profile="course"}
::::
:::: {.home-card .home-capstone}
[Apply to your own research]{.home-card-kicker}

### Your capstone project

Apply what you learned to organize, document, automate and share an analysis from your own research.

[The capstone](assessment/capstone-rubric.qmd){.home-card-link}

## Built on open material

This course began as a [mini-course at Stanford Biosciences](https://explorecourses.stanford.edu/search?q=BIOS+259&view=catalog&page=0&filter-coursestatus-Active=on&collapse=&academicYear=20232024)
([BIOS259, Winter 2024](https://github.com/asntech/bios259-w24/)), developed by Aziz Khan and taught with the help of
Alvina, Clemens and Brennan. It adapts and extends open lessons from
[NBIS](https://nbisweden.github.io/), [Software Carpentry](https://software-carpentry.org),
[Data Carpentry](https://datacarpentry.org/) and others.

Developed and maintained by [Aziz Khan](https://github.com/asntech/),
[Computational Biology and Cancer Regulatory Genomics (CBCRG)](https://khanlab.bio), MBZUAI.
